summary.learning_goal: Observe how closing bridges changes reachable delivery destinations and routes.
summary.primary_visualization: Isometric town split by a river, two bridges, moving vehicles and a status panel.
summary.primary_interaction: Recorded bridge closures produce blocked deliveries; reopening restores reachability.

strengths: Bridge status, map labels and unreachable counters agree in the captured disconnected state.
weaknesses: Routing optimality and the author-reported logic checks were not independently verified.

strengths: The two-bridge scenario exposes a concrete cause/effect relationship between connectivity and deliveries.
weaknesses: There is little explicit synthesis of the graph-theory concept or prediction guidance.

strengths: An isometric overview shows alternate crossings while close views show route segments.
weaknesses: Very small route and destination labels need a close camera view.

strengths: The sequence includes closure, disconnection and recovery with changed counts and routes.
weaknesses: Only an automated demo was obtained; response latency and free learner exploration are untested.

strengths: Bridge controls, fleet selection and dispatch log sit alongside the map they describe.
weaknesses: The side panel is information-dense and mobile behavior is unknown.

principles_to_learn: Let a learner remove a connection and observe which destinations fail.
Show topology, route changes and outcome counters together.
Make an intervention reversible so recovery can be compared.
Support both network overview and local route inspection.
things_not_to_copy: Do not claim shortest-path correctness without testing the algorithm.
Do not overwhelm the learner with a dispatch log before explaining the core connectivity problem.
golden_recommendation: Provisional demo reference. Use for network intervention, simulation, overview and detail. Live behavior remains unverified.
